Character codes index this 256-byte flag table. The engine copies the selected byte to $19 in its tile sampler at $247D.
One colour value for each character code. The room renderer at $520E looks up the character it just wrote to screen RAM before writing the corresponding colour cell.
Values indexed by the hardware sprite pointer. The object sprite staging routine at $2DC8 copies the selected colour into its zero-page hardware update table.

Eight groups of four frames, with eight character rows in each frame. The updater at $1EA8 cycles the group every call and advances the frame after visiting the eighth group. It writes the selected rows into the character graphics at $EFD8–$EFFF.

45 little-endian object template addresses. The engine patches its indexed load operand from the level setup table at $86B2. Consecutive distinct targets advance seven or eleven bytes across the records. Some indices share a target.

Sprite sequence bytes reached from an object template. A regular byte gives a sprite index. $FD requests an effect, $FE gives a delay and a sprite, and $FF rewinds by a word offset. This span occupies $B423–$B57B.
Four delayed sprite selections $80 through $83. Their durations are eleven, two, two and two. The rewind returns twelve bytes to the first command.

Sprite sequence bytes reached from an object template. A regular byte gives a sprite index. $FD requests an effect, $FE gives a delay and a sprite, and $FF rewinds by a word offset. This span occupies $B58B–$B596.

Object motion stream reached from a template. A regular pair gives a duration and two signed nibbles of motion. Zero changes the pointer to the next word, and $FD takes a sound effect number. This span occupies $B597–$B77A.
Three motion pairs followed by a zero opcode pointing back to $B77B.
